**Observation Log:**

[FACT] The user is trying to set boundaries with their social media use.  
[CHANGE] The user has been trying to limit their daily social media use to 30 minutes.  
[PREFERENCE] The user is following accounts that promote minimalism and digital detox.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant congratulated the user on recognizing the need to set boundaries with social media use.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that a 24-hour break from social media every week, also known as a "digital Sabbath," can have numerous benefits for mental and emotional well-being.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided five benefits of a 24-hour break from social media: recharge and relax, reflect and assess, gain perspective, improve focus and productivity, and enhance real-life connections.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested scheduling the break, planning alternative activities, setting up auto-responders, being kind to oneself, and reflecting and adjusting after the break.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant stated that the user's daily 30-minute limit is a great starting point and suggested tracking social media use for adjustments.  
[PREFERENCE] The user is considering deleting some social media apps from their phone to reduce temptation to mindlessly scroll.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant affirmed that deleting social media apps can be an effective strategy to reduce mindless scrolling.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided five reasons why deleting apps can help: out of sight, out of mind; reducing accessibility; breaking habits; reducing distractions; and increasing self-awareness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested identifying goals for deleting apps, choosing the right apps, finding alternative ways to access social media, preparing for FOMO, and replacing scrolling with healthier habits.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned alternatives to deleting apps, such as app blockers, website blockers, and app limitations.  
[FACT] The user previously deleted Instagram from their phone but reinstalled it after a week.  
[PREFERENCE] The user wants to find a better way to manage their motivations for using social media rather than just deleting the app.  
[PREFERENCE] The user has noticed they tend to post updates when seeking validation from others.  
[PREFERENCE] The user wants to use social media more intentionally.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided ten tips to help the user identify and change their motivations for using social media, including reflecting on posting habits, identifying emotional triggers, recognizing the validation cycle, replacing validation with self-awareness, and setting intentional posting goals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested creating a pre-posting checklist to evaluate motivations before posting.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant encouraged the user to find alternative ways to meet their needs and to celebrate small
